Classificazione di Stanford: tipo A se è:
Stanford classification: type A if the ascending aorta is involved (urgent surgical indication), type B if the dissection begins after the origin of the left subclavian artery (DeBakey III). The TEM classification (Type, Entry, Malperfusion) adds the site of the entry tear and organ malperfusion.
Distinguishing the lumens: the true lumen continues in continuity with the non-dissected aorta, is usually smaller and is denser in the arterial phase; the false lumen is larger, forms an acute angle with the flap (beak sign), may contain thin filaments (cobwebs) and opacify late or thrombose.
In the report: proximal and distal extent, maximum diameter of the aorta, from which lumen the celiac trunk, superior mesenteric and renal arteries arise, perfusion of bowel and kidneys, signs of rupture (pleural or mediastinal effusion, periaortic hematoma).
Complications that change management in type B: malperfusion, rupture or impending rupture, refractory pain or hypertension, aortic diameter ≥ 55 mm or rapid growth; risk factors for aneurysmal evolution: initial diameter > 40 mm, large or partially thrombosed false lumen.
In this case the pitfall is the false lumen that does not opacify: it may look like an intramural hematoma or a mural thrombus. Following it from above, where it is still opacified, and looking at the shape of the true lumen (crescent-shaped, compressed) clarifies that it is a dissection with a thrombosed or slow-flow false lumen; a delayed phase would distinguish thrombus from slow flow.
